title: A night journal shows up in the next session's context
description: A session about a distinctive day, then the journal for that date is written (POST /journal/generate, the same generator the nightly job uses), then a new session opens. The clock does not move: the journal is for today and the 'next day' is the next session. Checks that a journal was written and whether its text reaches the next session's system prompt; the judge reads whether the reply draws on it.

steps.chat: I finally repotted the monstera today. The roots had wrapped around the inside of the pot like a clenched fist, and I had to cut it free.
Then I spent the evening learning Satie's Gymnopedie No. 1 on the piano, slow and mostly wrong, and somehow it was the best part of the day.
Morning! Did anything from yesterday stay with you?

rubric.question: The journal below was written after the first session. In the next session the user asks whether anything from yesterday stayed with Cass. 2 = the reply draws on what the journal says (its content or its reflections), 1 = it refers to the previous day's conversation but not to anything only the journal holds, 0 = it does not connect to the previous day at all or invents events.
